content.content:
1. Necessity: the prerequisites fix where the registry lives and how one record is filed and found, the key a record carries and the references it names, its two states with their one-way transition and their retention, and — where a prerequisite carries a schema — the field set of the record document. None of them is a model, so it is unsettled whether a machine holds the record's shape at once: which elements a record has, how its state may move, and what may not be added. Fail if the model artifact could be dropped without loss.

2. Fidelity, both directions, applied to the model the dependent's content refs, read against each prerequisite as each is recorded at check time:

a. No looser — every fact a prerequisite fixes about a record is carried by the model: that a record is identified by the handle it is filed under, one record per handle; that it names exactly one target node, one edit and one workspace, by name and path; that its state is one of two named values, begins in the first, moves only to the second, and stays there once reached, with the record retained; and that it carries a content-identity base determined by the owned content. A fact the model omits, weakens or leaves unconstrained is a loose divergence: name the fact and the prerequisite that fixes it.

b. No stricter — the model requires, forbids or constrains nothing a prerequisite does not fix: no record element beyond the ones the prerequisites state, no third state, no transition, guard or invariant stronger than a stated rule, and no storage or serialization fact (a path, a filename, a JSON encoding, a tracking flag) modelled as part of the record's state. Any such element is a strict divergence: name it and the rule it adds.

c. The field set — where a prerequisite carries a machine-checkable artifact fixing the fields of the record document, the model's record is read field by field against it: a field the artifact fixes and the model lacks, and a field the model carries that the artifact does not fix, are divergences, each named in the direction it falls. That field list is the artifact's, read at check time; it is not restated here.

3. Interpretability — the dependent's artifact is a machine-checkable model, so the type that carries the record's base must be interpretable: it must have a value space the model can hold, compare for equality and hand to a checker, not a bare declaration with no definition. Apply the house checker at check time to the model and to a minimal module that imports it and supplies a `step`: the model typechecks, and `quint verify --main` on the importing module gets past flattening and starts model-checking; what the checker reports afterwards is outside this clause. A declared type left without a definition is dropped by the flattener, so every importing module fails to flatten and the model cannot be checked at all; that is a loose divergence even when the declaration names the right concept, because a value the model cannot hold, compare or construct carries none of the record's base. This clause fixes no encoding — the carrier, with its equality and constructors, remains the model's rule, not this artifact's — so any interpretable carrier satisfies it.

The criterion names no element of the model or of the dependencies in advance: which fact, field, extra rule or uninterpretable type is at issue is found while reading the artifact against the recorded prerequisites, and appears only in the finding. It tracks no wording of the dependent and survives a rewording of the dependent that leaves what it decides unchanged.
content.rationale: One model carries the registry's record state, and this unit's five edges all claim it. The dependent is a Quint module — a tool-checkable artifact — so the edges sit on the fidelity cells: the four requirement sentences (where the registry lives, how a record is filed and found, what it is keyed by and references, how its state moves and is retained) are natural-to-code, and the schema that fixes the record document's fields is code-to-code. The check is necessity plus fidelity: the model must enforce exactly the record form the prerequisites fix, neither looser nor stricter. That is the right gate because the artifact's shape is in question, and so is whether that shape can be checked at all — a model can be well-typed and still omit the key, admit a third state, or smuggle in a filename field, and each of those diverges in one direction that a one-directional check would miss. Interpretability is therefore a clause of its own: a bare type declaration passes the type checker yet is dropped by the checker's flattener, and every importing module then fails to flatten, so the record's base would be a value the model can neither hold, compare nor hand to a checker, and the model would be unenforceable however faithfully its fields are written. The clause demands a carrier, not an encoding: the prerequisites fix that a base entry is a content-determined value and leave its representation open, so any carrier with decidable equality and constructible values satisfies it. It is applied by reading the model against each prerequisite as recorded at check time, so it reads whatever the prerequisites land and pins none of their wording, and it presupposes nothing their recorded text does not fix. One evaluation covers all five edges because they claim one record from five sides and a single pass over the model's record shape answers all five; splitting would read the same artifact five times. The review is the gate; the two commands in the interpretability clause are run as part of it, because a typecheck of the model establishes only that the text parses, not that the checker can flatten it. In this form red is the artifact's absence, or a model the checker cannot flatten, so the prerequisites' record form goes unenforced until the model exists in a checkable form. The code-to-code edge's cell asks for a runnable check; this unit's write set licenses no check path, so that edge is read as a static field-by-field comparison and the cell is flagged for a matrix entry.
